description: We’re Delta-V Studios, on a mission to bring space exploration to life! 🚀 Combining stunning UI/UX, immersive gameplay, and real aerospace physics, we’re transforming complex space missions into an exciting, interactive adventure. Our goal is to inspire curiosity, challenge creativity, and bring students closer to the world of real space exploration. The countdown to launch has begun! 🌌
summary:
LAGRANGE: Deep Space Mission Design Academy is an interactive, web-based space mission simulation and engineering education platform built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Developed entirely in vanilla JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, and Tailwind CSS, the application operates as a self-contained, zero-asset procedural engine requiring no external media files. It uses 3D spherical lookup tables, value noise, and Fractal Brownian Motion shaders to render 60-FPS rotating celestial bodies, a 3D Gold-Kapton spacecraft, and Web Audio synthesized soundscapes in real time.

To make abstract aerospace trade-offs tangible for students, LAGRANGE couples real astrodynamics—including the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, inverse-square (1/R^2) solar flux attenuation, thermal and electromagnetic interference rules, and Deep Space Network link budgets—across four core modules: Interactive Physics Labs, a 22-part Spacecraft Builder and four-stage cinematic Flight Simulator, Rescue Broken Missions engineering puzzles, and a Solar System Sandbox featuring historical NASA fleet benchmarks. Players also manage limited budgets, unlock R&D upgrades, track commander profiles, and export verifiable PNG mission telemetry certificates
details:
1. What It Does and How It Works

LAGRANGE guides players through the complete lifecycle of a NASA deep-space mission across an onboarding sequence and four primary operational modules.

Interactive Onboarding and AI Flight Director (NOVA)

Players enter a Commander callsign, ignite a live 2D/3D Solar System Orrery Energy Core, and complete a 6-step configuration wizard to select their Experience Tier (Youth Cadet for ages 8–12, Flight Engineer for ages 13–16, Mission Specialist for ages 17+, or JPL Systems Architect), mission patch avatar, spacecraft neon trim, and physics mode (Guided Mode with formula hints or Realistic NASA Physics).

Module 1 — Interactive Physics Labs

Players conduct four hands-on visual experiments before building a spacecraft to master the governing equations of spaceflight.

1. Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation (Δv): Experimenting with specific impulse (Isp from 220 s chemical thrusters to 4,100 s Xenon ion drives) and propellant mass fractions against a 500 kg dry bus.

2. Inverse-Square Solar Flux (1/R²): Dragging a distance slider from 0.25 AU to 19.2 AU to observe how a 900 W solar array surges to 14,400 W near the Sun but drops below 4% of Earth's sunlight at Jupiter.

3. Thermal and EMI Cleanroom Adjacency Grid: A 3×3 spatial layout puzzle where players separate hot radioisotope generators (MMRTGs) from sensitive Thermal IR Spectrometers and apply Thermal Louvers and Faraday Shields to reach 0% interference.

4. Deep Space Network (DSN) Bandwidth: Simulating 15 GB science downlinks from 1 AU to 30 AU across UHF Omni, X-Band, and Ka-Band antennas linked to NASA's 70 m dishes at Goldstone, Madrid, and Canberra.

Module 2 — Spacecraft Builder and 4-Stage Flight Simulator

Players select from 8 NASA Mission Contracts and assemble a custom spacecraft from a 22-part hardware catalog while monitoring 6 real-time engineering gauges:

  • Budget Cap
  • Launch Mass
  • Orbital Reach (Δv)
  • Power at Target AU
  • DSN Data Link (kbps)
  • Science Objectives

Before launch, players can run an acoustic vibration and thermal-vacuum JPL Chamber Stress-Test, toggle a Planetary Gravity Assist Slingshot (+450 m/s Δv via the Oberth effect), or trigger Auto-Build for a verified baseline.

Launching initiates a 4-stage interactive flight cinema.

Stage 01 — Rocket Launch: Features a planetary synodic launch window alignment lock and a Max-Q first-stage separation timing bar, complete with retracting launch tower arms, water-deluge pad steam, Mach shock diamonds, vacuum plume expansion, and payload fairing jettison.

Stage 02 — Hohmann Orbital Transfer: Renders a live heliocentric or cislunar transfer ellipse with real-time velocity vectors, solar flux readouts, DSN link margin telemetry, and mid-flight crisis anomalies (Eclipse Shadow Cones, Coronal Mass Ejections, and Radiation Belt Surges) requiring tactical player decisions.

Stage 03 — Orbit Insertion and Retro-Burn: Simulates optical navigation target lock, a 180° attitude flip, and a gravity-well capture retro-burn into an elliptical science orbit.

Stage 04 — Planet Scan and Mission Ending: Players click pulsing surface target reticles to sweep the planet with a synthetic aperture radar swath, stream hexadecimal data packets back to Earth's DSN stations, unlock real scientific discovery logs, or witness visual failure forensics if their design violated mass, Δv, power, or bandwidth constraints.

Module 3 — Rescue Broken Missions

Players diagnose and repair four pre-built, flawed spacecraft designs:

  • The Overweight Lunar Lander
  • Blackout at Jupiter (5.2 AU)
  • The Cooked Infrared Camera
  • Marooned in Transfer Orbit

Repairs involve swapping launch vehicles, adding MMRTG nuclear cores, reconfiguring cleanroom thermal spacing, or upgrading to Xenon ion propulsion.

Module 4 — Solar System Sandbox and NASA Fleet

Features an interactive 0.25 AU to 30 AU orbital environment calculator that computes real-time solar flux in W/m², equilibrium planetary temperature in °C, one-way light-time delay to Earth, and recommended spacecraft architecture.

It also includes six inspectable NASA flagship mission profiles (LRO, MAVEN, Psyche, Europa Clipper, Parker Solar Probe, and Cassini-Huygens) that can be loaded directly into the Builder.

3. Benefits and Intended Educational Impact

Bridging Theory and Practice

Students rarely get the opportunity to experiment with an entire space mission from concept to operation, leaving trade-offs like exponential propellant scaling or deep-space power attenuation abstract. LAGRANGE turns those equations into immediate visual feedback.

Coupled Systems Engineering Thinking

Instead of isolated quiz questions, every hardware choice triggers realistic secondary effects.

Choosing a high-efficiency NEXT-C Xenon Ion Drive (Isp = 4,190 s) drastically cuts fuel mass but introduces a 400 W electrical draw and electromagnetic interference.

Flying to Europa (5.2 AU) renders standard solar arrays ineffective due to the inverse-square law, requiring nuclear MMRTGs and an 85 kg Titanium Radiation Vault, which in turn demands a heavier launch vehicle.

Learning Through Visual Failure Forensics

Players can launch non-compliant designs in Test Flight mode to observe the physical consequences of engineering errors, including:

  • A T+03 s launchpad structural overload explosion.
  • A Stage 3 Δv shortfall flyby into deep space.
  • Stage 4 frost crystallization during solar power starvation.
  • A DSN telemetry buffer jam.

Multi-Age Accessibility and Verifiable Output

With four age-calibrated experience tiers, guided formula tooltips, and an exportable 1200 × 675 PNG Official Mission Telemetry Certificate comparing the student's spacecraft against real NASA benchmarks, LAGRANGE works both as a self-paced game and a classroom STEM lab tool.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used

Core Languages and Styling

Built in a single, dependency-light HTML5 file using Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 Canvas 2D API, Inline SVG, and Tailwind CSS (3.4.17).

3D Per-Pixel Procedural Planet Shader Engine

Generates 512 × 256 equirectangular planetary textures at startup using 3D cylindrical Value Noise (VN3), 5-octave Fractal Brownian Motion (FB3), domain warping, and procedural crater-ray stamping.

A precomputed 3D Spherical Lookup Table (LUT / GEO / PST) maps surface normals, axial tilt, Lambertian terminator shadows, Phong ocean specular glints, and Fresnel atmospheric limb scattering at 60 FPS with zero external image assets.

Unified 3D Gold-Kapton Spacecraft CAD and Sprite Renderer

A single procedural geometry list (scPrims) drives both the interactive SVG blueprint in the Builder (scSVG) and the rotated 2D Canvas spacecraft in flight (scPaint).

It renders crinkled Gold-Kapton MLI thermal foil facets, a 5-segment white ceramic radiator spine, V-strut 3-panel photovoltaic wings, star-tracker baffles, optical ports, and a forward magnetometer boom.

Procedural Audio and Speech Synthesis

Uses the native Web Audio API (AudioContext) to synthesize all UI sound effects, rocket launch low-pass filtered white-noise rumble, and a multi-oscillator ambient space music engine with Biquad filters and stereo delay feedback (AM).

It also uses the Web Speech API (speechSynthesis) for live voice telemetry callouts.

Client-Side Persistence

Uses browser localStorage to auto-save Commander progress, XP, Level, Credits, unlocked R&D upgrades, completed labs and rescues, and mission history.

5. Creativity and Key Design Factors Considered

100% Zero-Asset Architecture

To guarantee instant loading, offline resilience, and zero broken media links for judges and classrooms worldwide, the team engineered every planet texture, nebula background, spacecraft model, sound effect, and music track mathematically in code without a single external PNG, MP3, or 3D model file.

Single-Screen Viewport Ergonomics (100vh Locks)

The team locked the Welcome screen, Energy Core, Onboarding Wizard, Flight Simulator, Physics Labs, and Rescue puzzles into a non-scrolling single-screen viewport (h-screen max-h-screen overflow-hidden) while preserving smooth scrolling on data-heavy catalogs like the 22-part Spacecraft Builder and 8 Mission Contract cards.

Long-Term Replayability via R&D Progression

Completing labs, rescues, and contracts awards XP across 6 NASA ranks (Cadet Flight Tinkerer to Legendary Chief NASA Architect) and Coins to unlock 12 R&D Upgrades, such as:

  • Graphene Bus Structures
  • Superconducting Heat Pipes
  • Faraday EMI Nano-Mesh
  • JWST Gold-Beryllium Mirror Skin
  • Deep Space Optical Laser Comm (DSOC)
  • Kilopower Fission Reactors
  • Voyager Golden Record
